question.problem:
Write $\frac{12{x}^{7}}{6{x}^{7}+4}$ in the form $a+\frac{b}{6{x}^{7}+4},$ where $a\ne 0.$
$12{x}^{7}$ $=$ {{field-1}} $+$ {{field-2}}
$6{x}^{7}+4$ $6{x}^{7}+4$
question.worked_solution:
First, we factor the numerator to put $6{x}^{7}$ in parentheses. Then, we add and subtract $4$ in the parentheses. This reveals a copy of the denominator without changing the value of the expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{12{x}^{7}}{6{x}^{7}+4} & =\frac{2(6{x}^{7})}{6{x}^{7}+4} \\  & =\frac{2(6{x}^{7}+4-4)}{6{x}^{7}+4} \\  & =\frac{2[(6{x}^{7}+4)-(4)]}{6{x}^{7}+4} \\  & =\frac{2(6{x}^{7}+4)-2(4)}{6{x}^{7}+4} \\  & =\frac{2(6{x}^{7}+4)-8}{6{x}^{7}+4}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we split the fraction into two, and then simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2(6{x}^{7}+4)-8}{6{x}^{7}+4} & =\frac{2(6{x}^{7}+4)}{6{x}^{7}+4}+\frac{-8}{6{x}^{7}+4} \\  & =2+\frac{-8}{6{x}^{7}+4}\end{aligned}
$$
